pure-announcement.rationale: This is a primary research report with a measured methodology and mechanism, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (shared-mental-model-erosion, agent-loop-telemetry, short-term-availability-tradeoff, agent-tool-ergonomics, code-mode-mcp, closed-loop-secure-codegen) cover the specific mechanism of AI-coding's atomic-task incentive eroding duplication, refactoring, connectivity and legacy-upkeep signals.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Claims are backed by a stated methodology measuring seven code-quality signals across a multi-year, multi-hundred-million-line dataset, with specific reproducible metrics per signal.

durability.rationale: The claim is a structural mechanism (AI's atomic-completion incentive trades off against long-term maintainability work) shown as a widening multi-year trend across four independent signals, not a single point-in-time percentage.

actionability.rationale: The report ends in five concrete practices a team can adopt directly: budget refactoring/legacy time, add duplicate-block tripwires, review for error-masking, coach where judgment is thin, and measure structure rather than volume.

atomicity.rationale: The core idea reduces to one coherent paragraph: today's default AI coding workflow rewards shipping atomic units while taxing invisible maintenance work, producing a measurable and widening maintainability gap that explicit tripwires and budgets can counteract.
